'''Klaus Müllen''' (born 2 January 1947) is a German chemist working in the fields of [[polymer chemistry]], [[supramolecular chemistry]] and [[nanotechnology]]. He is known for the synthesis and exploration of the properties of [[graphene]]-like nanostructures and their potential applications in [[organic electronics]].

== Early life and education ==
Müllen was born in [[Cologne]]. He studied chemistry there and was awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1971 under the supervision of Fabian Gerson at the [[University of Basel]]. He specialized in [[electron spin resonance]] (ESR) [[spectroscopy]] and his dissertation was on nuclear resonance and electron spin resonance spectroscopic studies on bridged [[annulenes]]. He completed post-doctoral studies at the [[ETH Zurich]] under Jean François Michel Oth (1926–2003) and received his [[habilitation]] in 1977 with a thesis on dynamic NMR spectroscopy and [[electrochemistry]].

== Research career ==
In 1979, he became professor of organic chemistry at the University of Cologne, and in 1983, he went to the [[University of Mainz]] as a professor. Since 1989, he has been director and scientific member of the [[Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research]]. In 2016, he became emeritus. Since 1995, he has been honorary professor at the University of Mainz and at the Gutenberg Research College of the University of Mainz.

His research interests are in the field of preparative macro- and supramolecular chemistry. Among other things, his group has succeeded in synthesizing and characterizing hitherto unattainable large polycyclic aromatics such as [[superphenalene]], which has a molecular mass of 1182 g·mol<sup>−1</sup> and consists of 34 condensed benzene rings.<ref name="Iyer Wehmeier Brand Keegstra 1997 pp. 1604–1607">{{cite journal | last1=Iyer | first1=Vivekanantan S. | last2=Wehmeier | first2=Mike | last3=Brand | first3=J. Diedrich | last4=Keegstra | first4=Menno A. | last5=Müllen | first5=Klaus | title=From Hexa-peri-hexabenzocoronene to"Superacenes" | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English | publisher=Wiley | volume=36 | issue=15 | date=18 August 1997 | issn=0570-0833 | doi=10.1002/anie.199716041 | pages=1604–1607}}</ref> 
[[File:Superphenalene.svg|thumb|Structure of [[superphenalene]]]] 
He has developed small disc-like organic building blocks using alkyl-substituted [[hexabenzocoronene]], and in particular HBC-C12<ref>Hexakis(''n''-dodecyl)-peri-hexabenzocoronene, dodecyl-substituted [[hexabenzocoronene]].</ref> – which self-assembles into crystalline liquid-phase structures (columnar liquid crystals) as potential [[organic field-effect transistors]].<ref name="Tsao Räder Pisula Rouhanipour 2008 pp. 421–429">{{cite journal | last1=Tsao | first1=H. N. | last2=Räder | first2=H. J. | last3=Pisula | first3=W. | last4=Rouhanipour | first4=A. | last5=Müllen | first5=K. | author-link3=Wojciech Pisula | title=Novel organic semiconductors and processing techniques for organic field-effect transistors | journal=Physica Status Solidi A | publisher=Wiley | volume=205 | issue=3 | year=2008 | issn=1862-6300 | doi=10.1002/pssa.200723401 | pages=421–429| bibcode=2008PSSAR.205..421T | s2cid=95330169 }}</ref> The considered two-dimensional benzene ring structures are examples of subunits of graphene lattices (graphene nanostructures). The graphene-like structures synthesized and investigated by Müllen include two-dimensional bands of less than 50 nanometers width with jagged edges. Of interest here are the electronic conduction properties and spintronics properties with a view to future replacement of silicon-semiconductor technology.<ref>[http://www.uni-mainz.de/presse/20443_ENG_HTML.php GRC Fellow Klaus Müllen receives Hermann Staudinger Award 2016] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190729152456/http://www.uni-mainz.de/presse/20443_ENG_HTML.php |date=29 July 2019 }}.</ref> In synthesis, he introduced a new method in graphene polymer chemistry: soft-landing mass spectrometry.<ref name="Räder Rouhanipour Talarico Palermo 2006 pp. 276–280">{{cite journal | last1=Räder | first1=Hans Joachim | last2=Rouhanipour | first2=Ali | last3=Talarico | first3=Anna Maria | last4=Palermo | first4=Vincenzo | last5=Samorì | first5=Paolo | last6=Müllen | first6=Klaus | title=Processing of giant graphene molecules by soft-landing mass spectrometry | journal=Nature Materials | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=5 | issue=4 | date=12 March 2006 | issn=1476-1122 | doi=10.1038/nmat1597 | pages=276–280| pmid=16532002 | bibcode=2006NatMa...5..276R | s2cid=25023497 }}</ref> Applications include synthetic light-emitting organic materials (such as OLEDs) and incorporation of molecular defects (defect engineering) organic analogues of semiconductor technology.

* 2010: Honorary Doctorate, [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]]<ref name="ae" />

* 2016: Honorary Professor, [[Beijing University of Chemical Technology]]<ref name="ae" />
* 2017: Member of the [[Academia Europaea]]<ref name="ae">[https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/M%C3%BCllen_Klaus Academy of Europe Müllen Klaus] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328123759/https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/M%25C3%25BCllen_Klaus |date=28 March 2019 }} accessed 30 July 2019</ref>
* 2017: {{ill|Hamburger Wissenschaftspreis|de}} (shared with Xinliang Feng)<ref name="Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina 2021">{{cite web | title=Klaus Müllen erhält den Hamburger Wissenschaftspreis 2017 | website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina | date=25 September 2021 | url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitglieder/mitglieder-im-fokus/klaus-muellen-erhaelt-den-hamburger-wissenschaftspreis-2017/ | language=de | access-date=18 November 2022 | archive-date=18 November 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221118183313/https://www.leopoldina.org/mitglieder/mitglieder-im-fokus/klaus-muellen-erhaelt-den-hamburger-wissenschaftspreis-2017/ | url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="cfaed 2017">{{cite web | title=Hamburg Science Award 2017 goes to Klaus Müllen and Xinliang Feng | website=cfaed | date=26 June 2017 | url=https://cfaed.tu-dresden.de/press-releases-201/hamburg-science-award-2017-goes-to-klaus-muellen-and-xinliang-feng | access-date=18 November 2022 | archive-date=29 September 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929213001/https://cfaed.tu-dresden.de/press-releases-201/hamburg-science-award-2017-goes-to-klaus-muellen-and-xinliang-feng | url-status=live }}</ref>
* 2023: Member of [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=中国新闻网 |url=https://m.chinanews.com/wap/detail/zw/gn/2023/11-23/10116533.shtml |access-date=2023-11-23 |website=m.chinanews.com}}</ref>
